notes: The count in the roadmap is a contract: the script always delivers exactly that many items and the end.recap repeats them in the same order. In multi-part scripts the roadmap also says which item lands in which part, and that promise is honoured by the handoff line.

Biology counts ITEMS (6 points, 4 विशेषताएँ, 9 points); physics and derivation chemistry count STAGES of a derivation (definition → formula → final expression) and never give a number. The announced count is binding — BIO-C1-LA-02 opens on 6 and closes on 'हमारे पूरे 6 points', BIO-C5-LA-03 closes on 'हमारे पूरे 9 points पक्के हो गए'.

Two shapes: the content roadmap ('पहले A, फिर B') and the outcome promise ('इस वीडियो के अंत तक आप ... सीख जाओगे'). For difference questions the roadmap names the comparison method ('side-by-side compare'), for preparations it promises the sequence ('आपको इसके तीनों क्रम से याद हो जाएँगे').
The roadmap must match the part split exactly; in every instance the count named ('दो parts में') equals the number of PART dividers in the file.

प्रश्न:
“प्रभावी परमाणु संख्या (EAN) क्या है? एक उदाहरण देकर समझाइए।”

notes: NEW because it is a distinct beat, not part of the board-year line. Note the restatement is LOOSER than the header: it glosses the Sanskritised exam wording into speakable Hinglish (परीक्षार्थ परीक्षण -> 'टेस्ट क्रॉस यानी परीक्षार्थ संकरण'). When the header carries 'अथवा' variants, only ONE is restated but the script answers the union of both.

NEW because the starter taxonomy has no id for it and it is load-bearing: BIO-C3-SA-01 later answers BOTH phrasings separately (अगर पूछा जाए X तो लिखो…). Devanagari technical term first, Latin gloss after (उल्बवेधन यानी Amniocentesis) — never the reverse.

New id: the starter taxonomy has no slot for reading the paper's wording back. It matters because the spoken restatement is where the question's own verb (समझाइए / सिद्ध कीजिए / अन्तर स्पष्ट कीजिए) enters the narration, and that verb drives the visual strategy. Note the restated wording is often the *cleaned* version of the header, not the header verbatim.

New id because the अथवा block changes what the answer must contain: BIO-C5-SA-05 teaches the whole mechanism AND opens with the bare definition so both phrasings are covered. PHY-C3-SA-03 carries four variants and reads none of them aloud. When the alternates differ in scope, the script covers the LARGER one and the smaller falls out of it.

Not in the starter taxonomy but present in 7 of 27. The readback is often paraphrased, not copied: BIO-C5-SA-02 inserts 'यानी Transcription' into the Hindi question so the English term is heard once before the explanation starts.

notes: The digit is written as a numeral ('4 नंबर') in every instance — it goes to a human reader, not TTS. Biology and Physics put the marks payoff at the END instead (see NEW.end.marks_banked), never in the opener.

The mark count must match the question's real weight — 4 for LA, 3 for SA. CHE-C3-SA-02 uses it as a BRIDGE instead of an intro (2 banked, 1 still to earn), which is the strongest version of the move because it makes Part 2 feel compulsory. Digits (4, 3, 2, 90%) are written as digits in these spoken lines; TTS will need them spelled out.

Recurs at the END too, as a closer ('आज के 4 नंबर तो पक्के!' CHE-C4-LA-01; 'बच्चों, 4 नंबर की तैयारी हो गई।' PHY-C2-NM-04), and mid-script as leverage to keep watching ('लेकिन पूरे 4 नंबर चाहिए ना, तो आगे के दोनों conversions भी उतने ही important हैं' CHE-C4-LA-01). The digits are written as digits in the source but must be spoken as words ('चार नंबर') for TTS.

The digit is always written as a digit in these drafts ('4 नंबर'), which violates the repo's no-digits-in-spoken-lines rule — a generator must emit 'चार नंबर'. Never mixed with a different number later in the same script: the intro promise and the end line always agree.

Always uses the PAST habitual (समझा था / देख लिए थे) for the recap and the PRESENT (आते हैं / करते हैं) for the new material. In physics the recap re-states the last EQUATION, not a heading, and is immediately followed by that equation's ON SCREEN block again.

NEW because bridge.recap_result covers only the heading-level version. This one costs 20–30 seconds of the part and is a deliberate trade: the reel survives being watched out of order. In CHE-C5-SA-08 it goes too far — Part 2 repeats Part 1's two examples and both ON SCREEN blocks verbatim, and the part has almost no new content.

In physics derivations the recap re-states the EQUATION reached, and CHE-C4-SA-02 and PHY-C2-NM-04 re-show the same ON SCREEN block and its spoken readout again — the parts are cut to be watchable out of order. Biology recaps name the stage/phase, not a formula. The recap is always 1–2 sentences; never longer.

In derivations the recap re-states the EQUATION reached, and the equation is re-printed as an ON SCREEN line immediately after (PHY-C2-NM-01 P2, PHY-C2-NM-05 P2 and P3), so a part can be watched standalone. notes: NEW and the single most important type for a generator. Two conventions: (a) PHY-C2-NM-02 and PHY-C2-SA-01 put a literal 'स्पोकन:' tag on its own line and transliterate EVERYTHING into Devanagari ('वी बराबर एक बटा चार पाई एप्सिलॉन नॉट'); (b) everything else uses a bare quoted line mixing Devanagari connectives with Romanised English maths ('E one बराबर है one by four pi epsilon naught'). Pick one per script and never mix. CHE-C3-SA-09 even reads the reaction aloud ('तीन N O गैस से N two O गैस') and flags the read-out with 'इसे पढ़ेंगे—'.

NEW and the single most mechanical move in the corpus. Three incompatible conventions coexist: (a) full Devanagari — ई वन बराबर एक बटा चार पाई एप्सिलॉन नॉट; (b) Devanagari frame with English numerals shouted in caps — TWO POINT THREE ZERO THREE बटे t; (c) full English — 'Potassium four, open bracket Fe…'. Physics uses (a) with the literal label स्पोकन:, chemistry mixes (b) and (c). Formulae are read letter by letter ('C o three plus', 'N H three'), never as a word. 'upon' and 'बटा/बटे' are both used for division, sometimes in the same file.

New id, and the single most important one for generation: NO digit or symbol is ever left for the TTS to interpret. Three dialects coexist — full Devanagari transliteration ('क्यू बराबर सी गुणा वी', PHY-C2-NM-04/PHY-C3-NM-02), English readout ('N H four N O two gives ...', CHE-C3-SA-07/CHE-C5-*), and a hybrid ('आर वन upon आर टू', 'की power one to ten'). Pick ONE dialect per script. Conventions: → is read 'gives', = is 'बराबर' or 'equals', / is 'upon', × is 'गुणा', brackets are spoken ('open bracket … close bracket'), subscripts become plain numbers.

THREE incompatible dialects, and a script must pick one and keep it: (a) Devanagari transliteration of Greek/Latin symbols — ‘सी बराबर एप्सिलॉन नॉट ए upon’ (PHY-C2-NM-05, labelled ‘स्पोकन:’); (b) English symbol names inside a Hindi frame — ‘V one बराबर है one by four pi epsilon naught K into q by BP’ (PHY-C2-NM-01, PHY-C3-NM-03); (c) full English spell-out for chemistry, with bracket structure said aloud — ‘Open bracket C o … close bracket, three plus’ (CHE-C5-SA-02, CHE-C5-SA-06). PHY-C1-LA-02 mixes (a) and (b) in the same file (‘डी-फाई-ई बराबर ई डॉट डी-एस’ next to ‘one by four-pi-epsilon-naught’) — that inconsistency is a defect, not a style. ‘×’ is read ‘into’, ‘/’ is read ‘upon’ or ‘by’ or ‘divided by’, ‘→’ is read ‘gives’.

The chain is always restated compressed at the end of the section (the 'मतलब' version), which is what the student writes. In chemistry the chain ends on the stability argument; in biology it ends by looping back to where the cycle started.

Every single algebraic step gets its own ON SCREEN block — nothing is done in the head. The verbs that introduce a step are a closed set: मान लो, रख देते हैं, common ले लेते हैं, बराबर कर सकते हैं, simplify करते हैं, cross multiplication करते हैं, neglect कर सकते हैं, divide करने पर. The approximation step is always flagged with hook.importance.

Equations are numbered and called back by number ('E का मान समीकरण (1) से यहाँ रख देते हैं') — so the numbering must be stable across parts. Cancellations are narrated as events ('4π और r² कट जाएगा', 'रो दोनों sides में cancel हो जाएगा'). Equations are plain-text Unicode (subscripts ₀₁₂, superscripts ⁻¹², ∮ ∝ ε π Λ κ), never LaTeX. No step is ever skipped — even ‘Q ऊपर और नीचे cancel हो जाएगा’ gets its own line. shape: <परीक्षा में|exam में> <इसे ऐसे ही लिखना है|बिल्कुल ऐसा लिख दोगे> तो <नंबर पक्के हो जाएंगे|नंबर मिलेंगे>
<इसे परीक्षा में बिल्कुल ऐसे ही लिखना, तभी पूरे नंबर मिलेंगे> / <क्रम उल्टा हुआ तो number नहीं मिलेंगे> / <इसे छोटा करके मत लिखना>।
परीक्षा में बिल्कुल ऐसा ही लिख दिया, तो आपके <N> नंबर पक्के।
यहाँ जो <main points|क्रम> बोलूँगा, इन्हें answer में ऐसे ही लिखना।

examples.text: और इसको अच्छे से समझना, बिल्कुल ऐसा लिख ​​दोगे तो परीक्षा में नंबर पक्के हो जाएंगे
★ "इसमें दो शब्द खास ध्यान रखने वाले हैं — 'पूर्ण' और 'बराबर'। इन्हें उत्तर में सही जगह लिख दिया, तो नंबर पक्के समझो।”
“इसे ध्यान से सुनना और याद रखना, क्योंकि परीक्षा में इसे ऐसे ही लिखोगे तो नंबर मिलेंगे।”
“ये पूरी line गाँठ बाँध लो और परीक्षा में ऐसे ही लिखना—द्विनिषेचन के समय ध्रुवीय केन्द्रक और नर युग्मक के मिलने से PEN बनता है।”
“सबसे पहले परिभाषा इसे परीक्षा में बिल्कुल ऐसे ही लिखना, तभी पूरे नंबर मिलेंगे”

notes: Often fused with hook.memory_aid in one sentence ('गाँठ बाँध लो और परीक्षा में ऐसे ही लिखना').

The negative form (नंबर नहीं मिलेंगे / number cut sakte hai) is used more than the positive, and is always attached to a specific failure mode: wrong order, abbreviated line, ratio without names. BIO-C4-LA-02 personifies the examiner (जाँचने वाला देखेगा), which no other script does.
In PHY-C1-LA-01 an editor footnoted this exact line '[b]remove' / '[c]NUMBER KAT SAKTE' — i.e. promising marks was being reined in. Generate it at most once or twice per part.
Two grammatical registers: तुम-form ‘लिखना’ in biology/physics, आप-form ‘लिखिए’ in the newer chemistry scripts. Keep one register per script.

types.label: N done, now the next one
types.description: Marks off completed items against the count announced in the roadmap, so the student always knows where they are.
when_used: Every counted list — parts of a structure, differences, properties, features, reactions.
Between items of any counted list, and at every part boundary of a counted script.
Difference and list questions, especially those spread over parts.
Any question whose answer is a fixed count of points, steps or factors — which is most of them.
shape: <चलो, एक हो गया?|दो हो गए|तीन गुण तो हो गए,> अब <दूसरा|तीसरा|चौथा और आखिरी> <part|अंतर|गुण>—<नाम>
<तो/चलो> <यहाँ तक> <N> <points/विशेषताएँ/प्रावस्थाएँ> हो <गए/गईं>। अब <अगला/N+1वाँ> <point>।
बच्चों <N> तो हो गए, अब आते हैं <अगले/last> <difference/point> पर—
<दो हो गए|स्टेप <n> भी हो गया> अब <तीसरा|अगला> <नाम>।

examples.text: “चलो, एक हो गया? अब दूसरा part—अध्यावरण यानी Integuments।”
दो हो गए तीसरा
“तीन गुण तो हो गए, लेकिन चौथा अभी बाकी है।”
बच्चों, 3 अंतर clear हैं, अब last वाला
"To bacho दो points हो गए

notes: The ordinal is Devanagari-spelled (पहला/दूसरा/तीसरा/चौथा) but the running total is often a numeral ('3 अंतर clear हैं') — inconsistent, and a TTS hazard.

Can count UP (दो हो गए) or DOWN (सिर्फ़ दो ही बचे हैं); the down-count appears near the end of a long list and carries an implicit 'stay with me'. Ordinals are always Hindi words (पहला, दूसरा, तीसरा, चौथा, पाँचवाँ, छठा), never digits.

The count is spoken in words sometimes ('चार तो हो गए') and digits others ('4 differences हो गए') — digits must be converted for TTS. Where the tally names the items done so far (BIO-C2-LA-02) it doubles as a micro-recap.

The count NEVER drifts: if the intro promised three, exactly three are counted out and the recap lists three. BIO-C2-LA-03 also uses a warmth variant, ‘तो यहाँ तक तो बेटा कर लिया! पहली प्रावस्था हो गई।’

types.label: This is where students go wrong
types.description: Names the specific error students make at this exact point, usually just before the correct version.
when_used: At confusable pairs (anode/cathode, Micropyle/Chalaza), at exceptions, and at the point a shortcut fails.
Before a fact with a near-neighbour: two similar numbers, two similar names, a suppressed allele, an ordering.
At sign/direction/order-sensitive steps and at confusable name pairs.
Wherever two terms differ by one syllable (शुक्रजनन/शुक्राणुजनन), two symbols swap (LH/FSH), or a unit/dependency is commonly inverted.
shape: <यहाँ|यहीं> बच्चे अक्सर <गलती करते हैं|confuse होते हैं|उलझते हैं> — <गलत रूप>, लेकिन…
<अब यहाँ थोड़ा ध्यान देना / और यहाँ बच्चे अक्सर गलती करते हैं> — <यहीं confusion होता है / यहाँ 100 में से 80 बच्चे गलती करते हैं>।
और यहीं पर <50% बच्चे / 100 में से 80 बच्चे> <उलझते हैं / गलती करते हैं> — <गलती क्या है>।
अब गौर करना, क्योंकि <क्यों घालमेल होता है>। <A> और <B> को एक मत समझ लेना।

examples.text: “यहाँ बच्चे अक्सर गलती करते हैं Micropyle को सिर्फ ‘छेद’ लिखकर छोड़ देते हैं, लेकिन…”
“इसे ध्यान से समझना, यहाँ 100 में से 80 बच्चे अक्सर गलती करते हैं।”
“यहाँ Micropyle और Chalaza को उल्टा मत कर देना—एक तरफ Micropyle, उसके opposite side पर Chalaza।”
यहाँ बच्चे अक्सर confuse होते हैं
इसे ध्यान से समझाना यहाँ 100 में से 80 बच्चे अक्सर गलती करते हैं।

notes: Never abstract: the wrong answer is quoted. Absent from all five formal-register scripts and from both no-year Physics derivations.
Always names the SPECIFIC error, never a generic 'be careful'. The flag is immediately followed by the correction — see NEW.teach.confusable_split, which is the correction half of this pair.

The statistic variant ('50% बच्चे', '100 में से 80 बच्चे') is always invented — no source. It is ALWAYS followed immediately by the correction, never left hanging. Never flag a mistake without resolving it in the next line.

The ‘100 में से 80 बच्चे’ statistic is invented and used as rhetoric — harmless, but a generator should keep such figures round and rare. BIO-C5-SA-02's instance is a correction of a claim the script itself might otherwise have made, phrased as ‘एक बहुत important correction’.

types.label: Pose the next question before answering it
types.description: Asks the question the next paragraph answers, usually starting from something that looks contradictory.
when_used: At the pivot from 'what it is' to 'why it happens', and before each new mechanism step.
Matching tables (each row asked as a question), mechanism questions (why does the size shrink?), and any 'reason' question.
Reason questions, and anywhere the textbook result is counter-intuitive.
‘क्यों’ questions, and the pivot into the ‘importance / uses / effect’ half of a two-part question.
shape: अब <असली सवाल|सवाल ये उठता है कि|सवाल आता है कि> — <प्रश्न>?
अब <सवाल है / असली game शुरू होता है> — <प्रश्न>? / <पहला/दूसरा>—<आइटम> किस <विटामिन की कमी> से होता है?
lekin अगर <तथ्य A>, तो फिर <विरोधाभास> क्यों <होता है>?
अब सवाल यह है कि <X> में ऐसा क्यों होता है? / अब आते हैं सबसे important हिस्से पर—<प्रश्न>?

examples.text: “अब असली सवाल —अवाष्पशील विलेय मिलाने पर क्वथनांक बढ़ता क्यों है?”
★ "अब सवाल ये उठता है कि ये एंटीजन बनते किससे हैं। यहीं से असली उत्तर शुरू होता है।"
अब सवाल आता है कि ³²P आखिर DNA तक पहुँचा कैसे? चलो, इसे भी समझ लेते हैं

अब सवाल है— आखिर ये size लगातार कम क्यों होता जाता है?
यहीं इसका सबसे important reason आता है।
“पहला—खून का थक्का न जमने की समस्या किस विटामिन की कमी से होती है?”

notes: Distinct from handoff.open_question: this one is answered within seconds, in the same part.
CHE-C10-LA-02 uses it seven times in a row to turn a flat matching table into a quiz — the single most reusable pattern in this corpus for list/match questions.

In physics the forward question is a quiz the teacher answers himself in the very next line ('बिल्कुल E और dS के बीच कोण 0° होगा'), which needs a beat of silence in the edit. In biology it is a genuine paragraph-level pivot.
Always answered within the next two lines — the question is a pivot, never a cliffhanger inside a part (cliffhangers only live at part boundaries, see handoff.open_question).

types.label: Build the mnemonic, don't just order it remembered
types.description: Supplies an actual memory device — a word-equation, an initial-letter pairing, or a stripped-down parallel list — rather than just ordering the student to remember.
when_used: Matching tables, long lists, and any set of numbers that must be kept apart.
Pairs that differ by one term (sucrose/lactose), isomer sets, and factor lists.
shape: <अक्षर/प्रतीक> मतलब <कीवर्ड>; <अक्षर> मतलब <कीवर्ड> … / बस <तीन शब्द> याद रखो — <A>, <B> और <C>। ये याद हैं तो बाकी उत्तर भी याद रहेगा।

एक छोटी-सी ट्रिक से याद रख सकते हैं—
<A → x + y>
<B → x + z>

examples.text: “चलो, अब पूरी table को एक आसान trick से दिमाग में बैठा लो—A मतलब आँख, D मतलब धूप और हड्डियाँ, E मतलब बन्ध्यता, K मतलब थक्का; C मतलब स्कर्वी, B₁₂ मतलब रक्ताल्पता और फोलिक अम्ल मतलब अरक्तता।”
“बस एक छोटी-सी trick याद रखो गुणन, वृद्धि और परिपक्वन। ये तीन शब्द याद हैं, तो बाकी उत्तर भी याद रहेगा”
और इसे याद रखने की ट्रिक - DNA की चौड़ाई 2 nm, एक पूरा घुमाव 3.4 nm और 10 क्षारक युग्म।”

★ "और अगर छह points याद रखना मुश्किल लगे तो ये तीन बातें याद रहनी चाहिए “लघुबीजाणु कई hote h और गुरुबीजाणु में सिर्फ एक क्रियाशील, चार लघुबीजाणु साथ रहते हैं और आगे परागकण, जबकि गुरुबीजाणु से भ्रूणकोष बनता है।”"

एक छोटी-सी ट्रिक से याद रख सकते हैं—
सुक्रोज → ग्लूकोज + फ्रक्टोज
लैक्टोज → ग्लूकोज + गैलैक्टोज

notes: NEW because hook.memory_aid is the imperative ('lock this in') and this is the artefact being locked in. Two distinct sub-forms: the SYMBOL→KEYWORD table (A मतलब आँख), and the FALLBACK SET ('if you can't hold six, hold these three'), which is what a student under exam pressure actually uses. Both are placed at the very end of the relevant part.

Distinct from hook.memory_aid: this one hands over a device. The device always drops the distinguishing detail deliberately (CHE-C10-SA-07's trick drops the D- prefixes that the correct answer needs — the script says so nowhere, which is a defect to avoid).

types.label: What to write, and in what order
types.description: Gives the structure of the written answer: which components to include, how many examples, what not to skip.
when_used: Just before the closing CTA, or at the end of a part whose content is one component of the answer.
shape: तो बच्चों, exam में answer लिखते समय पहले <A>, फिर <B>, और <C> जरूर <दिखाना/लिखना>। सिर्फ <shortcut> लिखकर मत छोड़ देना।

examples.text: "तो बच्चों, exam में answer लिखते समय पहले प्रभाविता के नियम की definition, फिर YY × yy का cross, gametes और F₁ generation जरूर दिखाना।"
“और exam में तीनों steps के नाम और reactions जरूर लिखना। सिर्फ final reaction लिखकर मत छोड़ देना।”
इस प्रश्न में परिभाषा के साथ दो-दो उदाहरण जरूर लिखिए, क्योंकि प्रश्न में प्रत्येक प्रकार के दो उदाहरण मांगे गए हैं।

notes: New id: this is the one move that talks about the ANSWER SHEET's structure rather than the content, and it is what the Notes-button CTA is handing off to. Always justified by the question's own wording ('क्योंकि प्रश्न में ... मांगे गए हैं').

types.label: These exact words must not be lost
types.description: Names the specific words, numbers or ordering in the sentence just spoken that the answer cannot survive without.
when_used: After a definition with technical qualifiers, after a dated/numbered list, and before any ordered preparation.
shape: बस यहाँ <N> words miss नहीं होने चाहिए—‘<w1>’, ‘<w2>’ और ‘<w3>’।

examples.text: बस यहाँ तीन words miss नहीं होने चाहिए—‘X सहलग्न’, ‘अप्रभावी’ और ‘विकार’।
★ "इसे पूरा लिखना खासकर ये तीन चीज़ें - पुटिकीय अवस्था, एस्ट्रोजन, और 5 से 13 दिन।"
ये तीनों नाम क्रम से याद होने चाहिए — क्रम बदला, तो नंबर गया।

notes: New id: hook.memory_aid compresses meaning, this one locks SURFACE FORM — the exact tokens the examiner's key contains. On screen it wants the words highlighted individually, not a restated sentence. The ordering variant ('क्रम बदला, तो नंबर गया') applies to preparations and stepwise processes.

types.label: Ask, then pause for the student to answer
types.description: Puts a small question to the student and leaves a beat for them to answer before revealing it.
when_used: One script only, on a Punnett-style prediction the student can actually make.
Multi-row comparison tables where each row follows the same pattern.
shape:
अब एक छोटा-सा सवाल—<प्रश्न>?
सोचो - सोचो
<उत्तर>
पहले <guess/predict> कीजिए: कौन <A> होगा, कौन <B> और कौन <C>?

examples.text:
अब एक छोटा-सा सवाल—लाल फूल वाले पौधे का सफेद फूल वाले पौधे से संकरण कराएँ, तो संतति में फूल किस रंग के होंगे?, 
सोचो - सोचो
★ "रुको, एक बार ऊपर वाली सूची से check कर लो । एलील ऊपर, एंटीजन नीचे — दोनों एक ही क्रम में चल रहे हैं। बस यही याद रखना है।"
सबसे पहले देखते हैं की चुम्बक के पास रखने पर तीनों का behavior कैसा होता है? पहले guess कीजिए: कौन प्रतिकर्षित होगा, कौन हल्का आकर्षित और कौन जोर से आकर्षित?
अब चुम्बकीय प्रवृत्ति का चिन्ह और परिमाण देखते हैं। पहले चिन्ह predict कीजिए: जो प्रतिकर्षित करता था उसका चिन्ह कैसा होगा?

notes: NEW and in ONE script only (BIO-C4-LA-01), which is also the most heavily rewritten one (★-marked lines). The second example is its sibling: telling the viewer to look back at the previous ON SCREEN block. Both assume the on-screen text stays up long enough to be re-read.

One file only, but used four times in it and it is the reason that script reads as teaching rather than dictation. Note it switches to आप-form imperatives (कीजिए, मानिए) for the prompt even though the rest of the script is तुम-form. The ON SCREEN card there is shown BEFORE the spoken row, so the prediction is answered by the screen.

types.label: ON SCREEN as an arrow flow, not a sentence
types.description: The on-screen block is a vertical chain of short labels joined by ↓ and →, or a numbered list with → mappings. It organises what was said; it never repeats the spoken sentence.
when_used: After any process step, any cause-effect link, and any 'A becomes B' statement.
Definition blocks, classification blocks, cause chains and quick-revision blocks. Near-universal in the 2024-25 biology batch and the formal chemistry batch.

ON SCREEN:
<पद A> → <पद B> → <पद C>
(या ऊर्ध्वाधर: <पद A>
↓
<पद B>
↓
<पद C>)

ON SCREEN:
<शीर्षक>
<पद 1>
↓
<पद 2>
↓
<पद 3>

ON SCREEN:
पूरी प्रक्रिया
जीन में उत्परिवर्तन
↓
HbS का निर्माण

↓

1. खण्डन → 2. प्रक्षालन → 3. अपचय → 4. ह्यूमीकरण → 5. खनिजीभवन
[ON SCREEN: अनावेशन → PbSO₄ जमा ↑ → H₂SO₄ सांद्रता ↓ → घनत्व  ↓]

आनुवंशिक विशेषक (Trait)

notes: Horizontal → for a sequence that fits on a line, vertical ↓ for a causal chain of 3+ links. ↑ and ↓ are also used INLINE as 'increases'/'decreases' markers, which is a different meaning of the same glyph in the same block (CHE-C2-SA-07). The arrow chain almost always restates the spoken sentence in 3-6 words per node — it organises, it does not transcribe.

Four spellings of the marker in this group: ‘ON SCREEN:’, ‘ON SCREEN’ (no colon), ‘On Screen:’, ‘ON SCREEN - ’. A parser must accept all four case-insensitively. ↑ and ↓ are used as VALUE arrows (MMR ↓ = the rate fell) as well as flow arrows in the same block — ambiguous, and worth disambiguating in generated scripts. Blocks are 3–8 short lines; nothing longer appears.

types.label: Closing revision table
types.description: A final on-screen block holding the whole answer as a table or numbered summary, read out loud item by item as the last teaching act.
when_used: End of the final part of every difference and list question.

notes: Rules visible in the data: (1) exam/meta vocabulary is ALWAYS English — exam, answer, definition, important, confusion, point, part, revise, trick, order, unit; (2) the textbook term is given Devanagari-first then English after यानी ('अध्यावरण यानी Integuments') — that pairing is a fixed idiom; (3) in the plain-language gloss the English word leads instead ('protective covering'); (4) numerals and formulae stay Latin/symbolic on screen but are spoken as words. Never write a Devanagari matra inside a symbol.

The rule is: Hindi technical term FIRST, English gloss second, joined by यानी or in brackets — never English first. Chemistry inorganic (CHE-C4-*) inverts this and runs mostly-English sentences with Hindi connectives, because the NCERT Hindi terms for d-orbitals are unfamiliar. Physics keeps English only for process words (simplify, condition, final result) and Devanagari-transliterates every symbol name (एप्सिलॉन नॉट, थीटा, ऐम्पियर).

Three levels: (1) Hindi technical term + English gloss after यानी — the exam-safe default; (2) English verbs/adjectives inside Hindi syntax (depend करता है, lose करके, clear हो गया); (3) whole clauses in Roman Hinglish (kahate hain, dhyan do, miss mat karna, yaad rakho) — these cluster in the informal hooks and handoffs. CHE-C4-SA-02 and CHE-C4-SA-06 push level 2 so far that numbers are English words inside Hindi sentences ('atomic number twenty four है'). NEVER glue Devanagari onto a symbol.

The X यानी Y gloss runs BOTH ways — Hindi-then-English for technical nouns (वंशागति यानी Inheritance) and English-then-Hindi where the English is what the student knows (GPP यानी सकल प्राथमिक उत्पादकता). Four files also carry Romanised HINDI, which is a typing artefact and not a style: ‘Ise’, ‘tarika’, ‘kyoki’, ‘aasani se लिख paoge’, ‘hi number milenge’ (BIO-C2-LA-03, BIO-C5-LA-01), ‘इस bar भी’ (CHE-C1-SA-02), ‘मजेदार तारिका’ (CHE-C4-LA-02).
